subject.title: [Bug]: message tool delivers text-only when inline keyboard is invalid (callback_data >64 bytes) — no error surfaced, reports ok

question: When requested presentation controls are removed by channel limits, should the message tool return successful delivery plus structured degradation details, or fail the entire send?
rationale: Both outcomes are defensible but define different public delivery semantics: preserving useful fallback text favors partial success, while fail-closed behavior favors strict interaction guarantees and may suppress valid text.

options.title: Return structured degradation
options.body: Deliver the safe fallback text but include machine-readable removed-control reasons so the agent can warn, retry, or choose a shorter action value.

options.title: Fail the whole send
options.body: Reject any send whose requested controls cannot be represented, guaranteeing all-or-nothing presentation at the cost of losing otherwise deliverable text.

options.title: Keep silent best effort
options.body: Continue reporting only the successful text delivery, accepting that callers cannot detect missing interaction controls.

recommendation.title: Return structured degradation
recommendation.body: Deliver the safe fallback text but include machine-readable removed-control reasons so the agent can warn, retry, or choose a shorter action value.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice changes the shared message-tool delivery contract across channel implementations, so repository-level product ownership is the best available routing point.
